headline: California bans companies from relying on AI to fire workers, also AI surveillance in bathrooms
summary: California's new legislation mandates transparency for AI-driven layoffs and prohibits using AI for employee surveillance in sensitive areas like bathrooms, setting a precedent for worker protection.
details: California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed new legislation aimed at protecting workers from AI-powered layoffs and surveillance. The laws are among the first in the nation to give employees specific rights regarding AI deployment in the workplace.

Specifically, the new bills prohibit employers from solely using AI for disciplinary actions or termination decisions. Companies are now required to provide transparency if an AI system is responsible for mass layoffs, relocations, or terminations.

The legislation also includes protections against AI surveillance tools in workplace bathrooms. Additionally, it prevents lawyers from fully delegating core legal work, such as drafting briefs, to artificial intelligence systems.

Newsom emphasized that AI should expand opportunities, not come at the expense of workers. The state's move follows reports of companies like Meta allegedly using biased AI tools for layoff selections, with one in four managers reportedly using AI for such decisions.

headline_marked: [[Google's Gemini 4 Argon outperforms Claude Opus and ChatGPT-6 Astra]] in new benchmarks
headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon outperforms Claude Opus and ChatGPT-6 Astra in new benchmarks
summary: The new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, boasts a 1M output token limit and has already shown significant internal savings for Google, outperforming rival models in various complex tasks.
details: Google has teased Gemini 4 Argon, its latest frontier model, which appears to outperform leading AI models from Anthropic and OpenAI. This new model promises sustained deep reasoning across complex workflows and delivers frontier-level performance.

Gemini 4 Argon is already being used in Google's internal workflows, fundamentally changing how the company operates. For instance, Argon agents applied memory optimizations across data centers, freeing up 300 TiB of storage space, with potential savings reaching 1 PiB.

Argon agents are also assisting in migrating Google’s C and C++ databases to Rush, processing tens of thousands of lines of code in core libraries. Quantum computing researchers have also leveraged Argon to optimize spacetime resources, beating published baselines by 40% in minutes.

According to benchmarks shared by Google, Gemini 4 Argon beat Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1, and ChatGPT-6 Astra across various tasks including knowledge work, ML engineering, and agentic coding. It also leads on the Vals Index, which measures AI models for economic value.

Alongside Argon's performance, Google is rolling out support for a massive 1M output token limit. This is a significant jump from the 64K token limit of previous Gemini models, enabling it to handle much longer and more complex tasks in a single response.
Gemini 4 Argon is not yet publicly available. Google is initially rolling out the model to trusted cyber defenders through its Fairwind Program to strengthen safeguards before a broader release.

After refining safeguards with tester feedback, paid API customers and Google AI Ultra subscribers will be the first in line. Introductory API pricing will be $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 95% discount on cached tokens, before doubling.
